question.worked_solution:
First, we divide the two functions, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{p(x)}{q(x)} & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(-2{x}^{4})}{(-\frac{8}{{x}^{6}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{{x}^{10}}{4} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }(\frac{1}{4}\cdot {x}^{10}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot {lim}_{x\to \infty }{x}^{10}\end{aligned}
$$

The graph $y={x}^{10}$ looks similar to an upward parabola, so

$$
{lim}_{x\to \infty }{x}^{10}=\infty .
$$

Multiplication by the positive constant $\frac{1}{4}$ does not affect the limit at infinity So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4}\cdot {lim}_{x\to \infty }{x}^{10}={lim}_{x\to \infty }({x}^{10})=\infty .\end{aligned}
$$
